chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from one of his companions, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'From the good fortune of a person is that his business is in his own city, and his companions are righteous, and he has children by whom he can seek assistance.'

key_terms.مَتْجَر: Business, trade, or place of commerce

ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of a person's good fortune according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) identifies three pillars of worldly prosperity: local commerce to minimize risk and cost, righteous companionship for spiritual and social stability, and offspring for familial support. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, reflects the practical socio-economic wisdom of the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that true 'sa'adah' (good fortune) is rooted in stability, community, and continuity within one's immediate environment.
